claims.CLAIM_TEXT_VERBATIM: Answers LAB-Q-0016 ('what structural biases would a future Job Posting Observatory carry?') as a design-stage pre-mortem, using exclusively this phase's own Observatory design (reports/lab_c0/LAB-C0-observatory-design.json); no platform was selected, no data was captured. Finding: yes, substantial and structurally unavoidable biases across eight dimensions. Platform selection: over-represents the eventually-chosen platform's own user base, under-represents employers using other channels (direct career pages, referrals, niche boards, or no formal posting at all). Sector coverage: over-represents white-collar/digital-native roles relative to informal, manual, rural, or micro-enterprise hiring. Geography: skews toward high-connectivity urban areas. Seniority: a near-certain skew whose direction is not determinable without data. Duplicates: the same vacancy can be counted more than once absent a platform-issued stable identifier -- disclosed and flagged by the design's own dedup taxonomy, not resolved by it. Posting persistence: long-lived postings are structurally over-represented by snapshot-design construction alone, independent of their true relative frequency. Employer self-selection: only employers who post formally, on a captured platform, are observed at all. Posting-vs-real-hiring divergence: structurally unresolvable by this design, since it never observes VACANCY or HIRE -- this is LAB-Q-0018's own separate, unresolved question. None of these biases block LAB-Q-0014 itself, which asks only what posting text alone can reveal; they must, however, be disclosed in full alongside any future LAB-Q-0014 finding.
claims.SCOPE_STATEMENT_VERBATIM: This claim states only which structural biases the proposed Observatory design would carry if built as specified, reasoned from the design's own properties. It makes no claim about any actual bias magnitude, does not resolve LAB-Q-0018's posting-vs-real-hiring divergence question, and does not authorize, execute, or provide evidence toward LAB-Q-0014.
LIMITATIONS_VERBATIM: Qualitative, design-stage reasoning only; no corpus exists, so no actual bias magnitude is measured or claimed
Seniority bias direction is explicitly left undetermined
Duplicate/evergreen biases are disclosed and flagged, not resolved, by the design's own taxonomy
Does not resolve LAB-Q-0018's own posting-vs-real-hiring divergence question
Does not authorize, execute, or provide evidence toward LAB-Q-0014, which remains unexecuted
Applies to the specific minimum-viable, single-pass design analyzed here; a materially different future design could carry a different bias profile
claims.WHAT_WOULD_UNSEAT_THIS_VERBATIM: Not literally falsifiable without a built corpus, since most of these biases follow near-definitionally from the design's own structure (single/few platform, public-listing-only, snapshot-based). A materially different future Observatory design (e.g. genuinely multi-platform, continuous, or supplemented by an independent hires-outcome source) would need its own, separate pre-mortem rather than reusing this one.

claims.PUBLIC_HEADLINE_ES: No se identificó una fuente admisible de avisos de empleo dentro del alcance y criterios evaluados (dos rondas, ocho candidatas y un chequeo de propiedad). No equivale a «no existe».
claims.CLAIM_TEXT_VERBATIM: LAB-Q-0014 ('which dimensions of a recruitment/selection process are observable using only public sources?') is closed INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE on source-availability grounds, without executing the question and without capturing a single posting. The path to this closure: LAB-C0 fully governed a minimum-viable Job Posting Observatory design (grain, coverage, temporal window, minimum fields, deduplication, provenance, hashing/versioning, reproducibility, retention, privacy, copyright/text-retention, ToS/robots/API compliance, rate limiting, inclusion/exclusion criteria) and populated this project's first-ever GENERATED_SOURCE governance policy (coverage, ethics, retention, reproducibility, bias, hashing, methodology), before any platform was investigated. Two bounded evaluation rounds then applied that governance, exactly as written, to eight named candidates plus one ownership-check bundle: LAB-C1 (Bumeran, ZonaJobs, Computrabajo, and the Cartelera Publica Central de Ofertas de Empleo Publico; ruling LAB-GOV-Q0014-PLATFORM-SELECTION-0001, NO_ADMISSIBLE_CANDIDATE_FOUND) and LAB-C1.1 (Remote OK, We Work Remotely, Indeed, and LinkedIn Jobs, plus a Konzerta/Multitrabajos ownership check; ruling LAB-GOV-Q0014-PLATFORM-SELECTION-ROUND2-0001, NO_ADMISSIBLE_CANDIDATE_FOUND). No candidate combining Argentina coverage, Terms-of-Service/robots.txt/API compliance, privacy fit, and reproducibility could be admitted: the private job boards (Bumeran, Computrabajo, and by shared-ownership inference ZonaJobs) carry explicit Terms-of-Service bans on automated access with no qualifying research API; the one Terms-of-Service-permissive candidate found in the first round, the Cartelera Publica, is blocked by a robots.txt disallow on the .pdf format carrying most of its postings and by a routine DNI-bearing privacy footprint that does not fit LAB-C0's incidental-contact-only PRIVACY provision; the two candidates with the most permissive Terms-of-Service/robots.txt/API profile found in either round, Remote OK and We Work Remotely, both fail decisively on Argentina-specific coverage; Indeed's own public API was permanently discontinued in 2023, leaving no admissible access mechanism at all; and LinkedIn carries an explicit Terms-of-Service scraping ban whose sole research exception is a competitive, sandboxed, aggregate-only program that would not supply individual posting records even if granted. Zero postings were captured across both rounds; zero scraping and zero API calls for data collection were made against any candidate. LAB-C0's own design and GENERATED_SOURCE policy were never redefined, loosened, or adapted to force any candidate's admission, in either round. Continuing to expand the search was assessed, at LAB-C1.1's own close, as carrying low marginal value relative to its scope-creep risk, given the structural diversity of failure modes already observed across eight distinct candidates. The conclusion is limited strictly to: no admissible source was identified within the scope and criteria evaluated -- this claim does not assert, and must not be read as asserting, that no admissible source exists at all.
claims.SCOPE_STATEMENT_VERBATIM: This claim states only that no candidate platform evaluated across LAB-C1 and LAB-C1.1, against LAB-C0's own governance gates, could be admitted as the Job Posting Observatory's source. It makes no claim that no admissible source exists anywhere; the conclusion is limited to: no se identifico una fuente admisible dentro del alcance y criterios evaluados (no admissible source was identified within the scope and criteria evaluated).
LIMITATIONS_VERBATIM: This is a documented incapacity to identify an admissible source within two explicitly bounded evaluation rounds, not a claim that no admissible source could ever exist -- a materially different future candidate, or a change in an already-evaluated candidate's own Terms of Service/API offering, could unseat it
No new platform research was conducted to produce this claim; it formalizes LAB-C1's and LAB-C1.1's own already-recorded findings into the claim-ledger's terminal lifecycle
Does not reopen, alter, or re-litigate any individual candidate's own GATE_RESULT from LAB-C1 or LAB-C1.1

Does not modify LAB-Q-0014's own ledger STATUS field (remains NOT_YET_OPERATIONAL), per this project's own established convention that a question's registered STATUS is never rewritten post-hoc when a claim resolves it (precedent: LAB-Q-0004/0005/0008/0009/0010/0012/0016)
Does not affect LAB-Q-0015/LAB-HYP-0008, LAB-Q-0016, LAB-Q-0017, or LAB-Q-0018, none of which depend on this claim or on any Job Posting Observatory capture
Treated as this project's terminal disposition for LAB-Q-0014 given the search conducted; not a claim that no future evidence could ever unseat it
claims.WHAT_WOULD_UNSEAT_THIS_VERBATIM: Discovery and governed evaluation of a genuinely new candidate not considered in LAB-C1 or LAB-C1.1 (e.g. a sector-specific Argentine board, an employer-side ATS with a public research feed, or a future official open dataset of individual job postings), or a material change in an already-evaluated candidate's own Terms of Service, robots.txt, or API offering (e.g. a private board publishing a public research-scoped API, or the Cartelera Publica moving its convocatorias to a non-PDF, robots.txt-permitted format) -- none of which is pursued or expected by this claim.

claims.PUBLIC_HEADLINE_ES: No hay evidencia suficiente, dentro de las fuentes y el alcance evaluados, para comparar avisos publicados con resultados reales de contratación: sin corpus de avisos, sin fuente de eventos de contratación y sin vinculación validada.
claims.CLAIM_TEXT_VERBATIM: LAB-Q-0018 ('when both are observable, how do descriptions based on published job postings diverge from descriptions based on real hiring outcomes?') is closed INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE on source-availability grounds, without any new research and without measuring or estimating any divergence. The question's own IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS demand, simultaneously: (1) an admissible JOB_POSTING corpus (LAB-OBJ-0019); (2) an independent source of HIRE events (LAB-OBJ-0022); and (3) a valid mechanism to compare or link the two. None is met within the sources and scope evaluated. (1) No admissible postings corpus exists: LAB-C1 and LAB-C1.1 evaluated eight candidates plus an ownership-check bundle against LAB-C0's own governance, applied as written, and both ruled NO_ADMISSIBLE_CANDIDATE_FOUND; LAB-Q-0014 was closed INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE on that limitation (LAB-CLM-0013); no posting was captured. (2) No admitted source observes HIRE events: LAB-OBJ-0022 remains DEFINED_PENDING_SOURCE with no observation mechanism, the Job Posting Observatory is NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR HIRE (LAB-SCM-0024) and was designed never to observe hiring outcomes, and LAB-B1 found no registration-flow (altas/bajas) data in any ARCA publication evaluated. Employment stocks (EMPLOYMENT_RELATIONSHIP, LAB-OBJ-0003) were not reinterpreted as hiring events, because HIRE is the transition event and not the resulting stock. (3) No validated linkage or common taxonomy connects the two sides: no admitted source shares a person-level or employer-level identifier with any other (LAB-CLM-0003, LAB-CLM-0011), and MLER's EMPLOYER/JOB fields are unrealized (GOV-006). The object-model distinctions POSTING != VACANCY != HIRE were preserved throughout: a posting was never treated as a vacancy, a vacancy was never treated as observable, and neither was treated as a hire. Because the question is conjunctive (both sides must be observable), the absence of either side alone would suffice; here both are absent. The conclusion is limited strictly to: there is not sufficient evidence, within the sources and scope evaluated, to compare postings with real hiring outcomes. This claim does not assert, and must not be read as asserting, that such evidence cannot exist outside this project's scope, and it deliberately does not use NOT_IDENTIFIABLE, which would assert a stronger structural impossibility than the current evidence supports.
claims.SCOPE_STATEMENT_VERBATIM: This claim states only that no evidence sufficient to compare descriptions based on published job postings with descriptions based on real hiring outcomes exists within the sources and scope evaluated. It does not assert that such evidence cannot exist outside this project's scope. In Spanish, as scoped: no existe evidencia suficiente dentro de las fuentes y alcance evaluados para comparar postings con resultados reales de contratacion.
LIMITATIONS_VERBATIM: This is a documented insufficiency of evidence within the sources and scope evaluated, not a claim that such evidence cannot exist outside this project's scope
No new source discovery, RAW reading, or data capture was performed to produce this claim; it formalizes already-recorded findings into the claim ledger's terminal lifecycle
The hire-side absence rests on this project's own admitted sources and prior searches; V1 manifests were not inspected for flow series in this block
Does not assert NOT_IDENTIFIABLE; no structural impossibility of the comparison is claimed
Does not measure or estimate any postings-versus-hires divergence in either direction
Does not modify LAB-Q-0018's own ledger STATUS (remains NOT_YET_OPERATIONAL), per this project's convention that a question's registered STATUS is never rewritten post-hoc when a claim resolves it
Does not affect LAB-Q-0014 (closed, LAB-CLM-0013), LAB-Q-0015/LAB-HYP-0008 and LAB-Q-0017 (NOT_IDENTIFIABLE), or LAB-Q-0016 (closed, LAB-CLM-0012)
claims.WHAT_WOULD_UNSEAT_THIS_VERBATIM: Governed admission of an admissible JOB_POSTING corpus together with an independent source of HIRE events (transition or flow data, not employment stocks) and a validated linkage or taxonomy connecting them -- none of which is pursued or expected by this claim, and each of which would require its own separately authorized admission.
